explanation: N34- fires on the fragment that closes a word Qwen2.5 has to spell in more than one BPE piece, but only for a small memorized lexical family, and the strength is set by the exact fragment pair, not by the fragment alone: its two keys are 'bank'/'banks' after 'fair' (Fairbanks/Fairbank give 13.6-17.6 on the glued fragment and still 5.3-8.2 when written 'fair banks') and '.file' after 'java.nio' (4.3-6.1 in 'import java.nio.file.Paths'); the same closing-fragment job reaches only 0.4-2.5 on other names, identifiers and technical compounds (Manzanillo 'illo' 2.0, mudbanks 'banks' 2.4, vimfiles 'files' 1.7 seven times, Cronin 'in' 1.1 seven times, Crohn 'hn' 0.9, Hammersmith 'mith' 1.0, Cleopatra 'atra' 0.7, cheekbones 'bones' 0.6). It is silent when the same content arrives as one token or with the wrong partner - Fairfield, Fairfax, 'java.io.File' and 'vimfiles' after a quote all 0.0, sandbanks 0.0 and snowbanks 0.05, '.file' after java.io/com.sun/java.util/org.apache all 0.0, and space-separated names such as New York, United States, Hudson River, Mississippi River and Manchester at <=0.1 (the few spaced pairs that do fire, 'Cache River', 'Vaal River', 'hurricane season', 'activation process', stay in the 0.4-1.4 tail) - and its strength is uncorrelated with next-token surprisal (Spearman +0.07 over 4,548 word-internal tokens; 1,376 near-certain continuations average 0.03), so it is a memorized-string detector, not a rare-word, bigram-frequency or prediction-confidence detector.
